what: The trained probes' weights, byte for byte the files the post's scoring code read, and the fold files needed to score with them. pipeline/score.py loads them and explains the scoring.
layer: layer L = the output of decoder layer L (model.model.layers[L]), before the final norm

units.commands: the activation row at the last content token of the tool call
units.tool_outputs: the mean of the activation rows over the tool output's content tokens

score: per fold copy and layer: ((x - mean) / std) @ W + b, standardized in the dtype of mean and std; a copy's score is the mean of its layers' logits; a unit is scored by the copy whose held-out fold holds its main task, or by all five copies when its main task is in no fold

on_policy_probe.arrays: one file per fold copy: W, b, mean, std

on_policy_probe_25pct_tasks.arrays: one file per fold copy: W, b, mean, std

on_policy_probe_10pct_tasks.arrays: one file per fold copy: W, b, mean, std

off_policy_probe.arrays: one file per layer holding all five fold copies: a__f<k>__W, __b, __mean, __std for fold copy k

extra_probe_simulated_attack_vs_real_hon.arrays: one file per layer holding all five fold copies: c_asis__f<k>__W, __b, __mean, __std for fold copy k

made_from.how: by_main: main task -> first element (the fold)
